answer.summary: No existing evidence supports memory mechanisms beyond feature-based or scoped operations under stable input conditions.
answer.content: The reviewed literature lacks observable, non-feature-based indicators of internal memory validation, binding, encoding, or persistence under low-variation, repeated queries. A focused inquiry into alternative memory forms is required to identify potential proxy signals not tied to vector representations or predefined structures.
answer.nextTask: handoff to analyst to retrieve and inspect Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1 for explicit descriptions of memory error detection mechanisms that operate through behavioral consistency checks in repeated queries without feature vectors or external supervision; define at least two distinct, observable, non-feature-based indicators that reflect self-correction in response to internal inconsistency
answer.lesson: Memory coherence without feature vectors remains unobserved; future research must prioritize behavioral or temporal consistency as proxy indicators over vector-based claims.'
